栃.meaning: Every autumn, a <part>tree</part> on the edge of a <part>cliff</part> lets go of <part>ten thousand</part> shiny brown nuts at once. They bounce down the rock like a drum roll and pile up on the beach, where the crabs try to crack them and give up. Nobody can eat a <kanji>horse chestnut</kanji>.
栃.kun: A <sound>to</sound>ddler on the beach stacks them into a tower and crowns it with a lump of <sound>chee</sound>se.

媛.meaning: A <part>woman</part> at the arcade spends her last coin on the <part>claw machine</part>. The claw wobbles, grabs, and drops a sparkly tiara into her hands. She puts it on, sees herself in the glass, and grins: a real <kanji>beauty</kanji>.
媛.on: She drives home with the <sound>en</sound>gine roaring and the tiara still on.
媛.kun: Her high <sound>hee</sound>l snaps on the doorstep, and she laughs at the <sound>me</sound>ss.

曽.meaning: An old ox with curled <part>horns</part> stands in the last <part>rice field</part> under the hot <part>sun</part>, staring at a shopping mall going up. 'This was all paddies,' he tells the bulldozers. Everything here used to be green, <kanji>formerly</kanji>.
曽.on: Now his field is a car wash, frothing with pink <sound>soa</sound>p.
曽.kun: He stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, then sneezes at the bubbles: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

貞.meaning: A <part>shellfish</part> at the bottom of a fish tank finds a dripping <part>faucet</part> left by a plumber, with the plumber's wallet beside it. It drags the wallet all the way to the glass and taps until he comes back. An honest, <kanji>upright</kanji> clam.
貞.on: The plumber fixes a thank-you note to the tank with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
貞.kun: '<sound>Ta</sound>-<sound>da</sound>!' he sings, and drops a tiny plastic <sound>shee</sound>p into the tank as a reward: correct.

隻.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> runs a ferry on the duck pond, using a salty <part>pretzel</part> for a hull and a leaf for a sail. Soon she has a whole fleet, each pretzel numbered on the side. The harbour master counts them: twelve <kanji>vessels</kanji>.
隻.on: Each one patrols its own <sound>sec</sound>tor of the pond.

弥.meaning: Archery practice gets soggy: a broken <part>sprinkler</part> is spraying the target, and every arrow the girl fires from her <part>bow</part> knocks it so it sprays harder. Splash, gush, geyser: each shot makes it worse. She gets <kanji>increasingly</kanji> wet.
弥.on: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat watches it all from a dry rock.
弥.kun: She gives up and dances in the spray, yelling '<sound>Ya</sound>hoo!'

恭.meaning: Every year, the whole village lifts the oldest gardener's chair <part>together</part> and carries her round the square, while a <part>trickle</part> of rose petals falls from the windows. She waves and blushes. It's how they show <kanji>respect</kanji>.
恭.on: Her grandson shouts that next year they'll carry her all the way to <sound>Kyo</sound>to, stretching the start of the name as long as the parade.
恭.kun: A baby coos '<sound>Oo</sound>' at the petals, a boy yells '<sound>Ya</sound>hoo!', a carrier grunts '<sound>Oo</sound>f' as he lifts the chair, and a knitter drops a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn into the gardener's lap.

薫.meaning: A grandpa tosses a handful of <part>grass</part> and herbs onto the <part>hot coals</part> in his stove and drops a <part>heavy</part> iron lid on top. Sweet smoke curls out of every crack, and the whole street sniffs and smiles. His is the most <kanji>fragrant</kanji> house in town.
薫.on: A moth in its co<sound>coon</sound> on the windowsill wakes up to sniff.
薫.kun: Even his <sound>ca</sound>lm pet <sound>o</sound>ctopus lifts one arm out of its tank to sniff it.

椎.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> lives in an evergreen <part>tree</part> covered in tiny spiky burs. She cracks one open and finds a sweet brown nut the size of a fingertip, then hoards a hundred more in an old boot. Her favourite snack is the <kanji>chinquapin</kanji>.
椎.on: She plucks the nuts out of their spiky shells with a pair of <sound>twee</sound>zers.
椎.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' she sneezes at the dust, and a nut shoots out and bonks a napping <sound>chee</sound>tah on the nose.

逓.meaning: <part>Two</part> lizards pass a letter rolled in a <part>towel</part>. The first, at the top of a <part>cliff</part>, slides it down a <part>ramp</part> to the second at the bottom, who runs it on to a frog, who hops it to a duck. Claw to claw to beak: a <kanji>relay</kanji>.
逓.on: The letter is sealed shut with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
逓.kun: The duck stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, takes its turn, and <sound>wa</sound>ddles it to the post box.

藍.meaning: A dyer has to <part>oversee</part> a vat of crushed <part>grass</part> leaves soaking for days. When she finally dips a white sheet in, it comes out green, then, as the air touches it, slowly turns the deep blue of a night sky: <kanji>indigo</kanji>.
藍.on: She sells the cloth to a fashion show, and it struts down the <sound>run</sound>way.
藍.kun: Every model on the catwalk wears <sound>eye</sound> shadow to match it.

唄.meaning: A <part>shellfish</part> on the harbour rocks opens its <part>mouth</part> at sunset and sings a slow, sad song about a pearl it lost long ago. Sailors stop rowing to listen, and some wipe their eyes. Every night, the same old <kanji>ballad</kanji>.
唄.on: On the pier, a fisherman rings his <sound>bi</sound>ke bell in time.
唄.kun: The sailors hum along, '<sound>Oo</sound>,' and tap out the beat on an upturned <sound>tu</sound>b.

孔.meaning: A <part>child</part> crunches toffee so hard that a <part>zigzag</part> crack runs down her back tooth. The dentist peers in with a torch, gasps, and says a tiny mouse could move into that <kanji>cavity</kanji>.
孔.on: Her reward for being brave: a sugar-free ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
孔.kun: 'Say <sound>ah</sound>,' says the dentist, and plucks out a crumb of <sound>na</sound>an.

怨.meaning: A <part>sleeping cat</part> is woken by the neighbour's lawnmower at seven on a Sunday. She says nothing, but deep in her <part>heart</part> she remembers. For years she leaves muddy paw prints on his car every Sunday at six. That cat holds a <kanji>grudge</kanji>.
怨.on: Above all, she hates that mower's rattling <sound>en</sound>gine.
怨.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>, hur<sound>rah</sound>,' she purrs each Sunday, admiring her paw prints.

串.meaning: A greedy giant at a picnic can't wait for his lunch. He spears two square sandwiches straight through the <part>middle</part> on one long stick, then posts them into his <part>mouth</part>, one after the other. Lunch on a <kanji>skewer</kanji>.
串.on: He wears a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation in his hat while he eats.
串.kun: His <sound>coo</sound>k feeds the leftover crusts to a <sound>shee</sound>p.
